newsitem.title: THAILAND: Jinxed wooden elephants blamed for Amnuay quitting.
newsitem.headline: Jinxed wooden elephants blamed for Amnuay quitting.

text.p: While some officials believe political infighting led to the departure of Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on Thursday, others blamed it on the return of two decorative wooden elephants at the ministry's entrance.
The two life-sized elephants were ordered out of the ministry and sent to various temples in 1990 by then-finance minister Banharn Silpa-archa, who believed they were jinxed.
"But early this month, the wooden elephants returned ... and once they came back all the bad things have happened," one teary-eyed ministry official told reporters.
"These elephants were away for several years but once they returned a good man has to go. I now believe that there is a jinx in them," he added.
Thais are mostly Buddhists, but superstition is also common in this land of elephants.
Amnuay quit after political conflicts with some rivals in the six-party coalition government of Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, political sources said.
His departure has rocked Thailand's already weak stock market and hammered the baht currency.
